name: FORGE
expansion: Functional-posterior Observatory for Refinement and Geometric Exploration

intro.problem: FORGE, the posterior observatory built as a capstone, splits a model's predictive variance into a reducible epistemic part and an irreducible aleatoric part [@kendall2017][@hullermeier2021]; applied to the ATLAS long-lived-particle networks, it has so far raised more questions than it has answered.
intro.value: Knowing which events, regions and networks are data-limited rather than at their physical limit would show the analysis where more simulation, better features or a different architecture would pay off, and would put an honest uncertainty on the background estimate itself.
intro.approach: The fast path is a last-layer Laplace approximation [@mackay1992][@kristiadi2020][@daxberger2021], checked against Hamiltonian Monte Carlo [@neal2011][@hoffman2014][@izmailov2021]. On the ATLAS networks the two disagree in unexpected ways, the epistemic-to-aleatoric ratio readings have not been examined, and the method needs networks with specific properties that TRUSS may change.
intro.goals: The next phase explains the Laplace-versus-sampler discrepancies, reads the ratio metrics for the analysis networks, adapts FORGE to whatever architectures TRUSS produces, and works out how its metrics fit into the rest of the research program.

questions: Why does the fast Laplace path disagree with the sampler on the ATLAS networks, and where?
What do the epistemic-to-aleatoric ratios say about the analysis networks: data-limited, or at their limit?
How should FORGE's metrics feed the other projects, and does it have to change to analyze the networks TRUSS generates?

open.text: The fast Laplace path over-states epistemic variance against the sampler on every board tested; no correction has been applied.
Rank-based input scaling rescued heavy-tailed features that min-max scaling silently flattened; not yet carried into the current analysis line.
Selecting checkpoints on the fold being graded biases the reported metric; the current trainers have not been audited for it.
The public site serves only the splash; the dashboard is built but not wired in behind it.

timeline.label: Capstone opens: Bayesian posterior observatory proposed
Base measure locked: variance decomposition, four metrics
ATLAS networks ported to FORGE; mode and fold-pooling bugs found and fixed

components.name: Laplace versus sampler
components.subtitle: The unexplained discrepancies
components.summary: The fast approximation and the reference sampler agree in some regions of the ABCD plane and not in others, and the gap is not yet understood. The first job is to explain it before trusting either reading.

items.label: Where
items.detail: Agreement in the high-score regions, over-statement of epistemic variance in the low-score ones

items.label: Space
items.detail: Readings in logit space and in probability space disagree, so the two must be reconciled before a ratio is quoted

items.label: Checks
items.detail: Sampler convergence diagnostics and a dispersed second chain, as done for the other experiments [@izmailov2021]

components.name: Ratio metrics
components.subtitle: Epistemic-to-aleatoric, not yet read
components.summary: FORGE reports the ratio of epistemic to aleatoric variance per event and per region. These readings exist for the ATLAS networks but have not been examined or compared across the loss configurations.

components.name: Network requirements
components.subtitle: What FORGE needs from a model
components.summary: FORGE can only analyze networks that meet certain conditions. The current analysis networks were adapted to meet them; architectures from TRUSS may not, so FORGE may need to adapt in turn.

items.label: Declared likelihood
items.detail: Each network a Bernoulli model over the label; the two-network objective is a composite likelihood [@varin2011]

items.label: True mode
items.detail: The last layer refit to the actual posterior mode before the approximation is taken [@mackay1992]

items.label: One basis
items.detail: One bundle per cross-validation fold, never pooled across folds

items.label: Sampler reach
items.detail: A last layer small enough for the reference sampler to mix

items.label: Penalties
items.detail: Whether decorrelation and closure terms belong in the posterior curvature is still open

components.name: Token-structured head
components.subtitle: Attention upstream, Laplace on top
components.summary: The Laplace approximation constrains only the last map, so anything upstream can be nonlinear, an attention trunk included. Reading the concatenated per-feature token states instead of one pooled vector gives a larger last layer with structure the observatory can use, while staying within the sampler's reach [@gorishniy2021].

items.label: Token allocation
items.detail: The existing per-dimension allocation of epistemic variance, summed within each token: an exact share per input feature that still adds to the total

items.label: Two attributions
items.detail: Token allocation read against the attention maps; agreement counts as evidence, disagreement points at attention [@jain2019]

items.label: Focus versus doubt
items.detail: Whether events with diffuse attention carry more epistemic variance, with uncertainty-aware attention as the reference design [@heo2018]

items.label: Matched comparison
items.detail: Plain and attention networks compared on the ratio metrics at matched discrimination, with the curvature check for saturation first

items.label: Scope
items.detail: Attention weights stay point estimates; the decomposition covers the head only, so the known over-confidence of last-layer methods carries over

components.name: Fit with the program
components.subtitle: Not yet examined
components.summary: How FORGE's outputs plug into the other projects has not been worked out.

results.title: The approximation over-states uncertainty
results.text: Against the sampler, the fast Laplace path over-states epistemic variance on every board tested; on the ATLAS networks it agrees in the high-score regions and over-states in the low-score ones.

results.title: The reading depends on the space
results.text: Epistemic variance computed in logit space and in probability space give different ratios for the same network, so no ratio is quoted until the two are reconciled.

results.title: Porting found real bugs
results.text: A trained network is not at its posterior mode, and folds cannot be pooled into one posterior; both had to be fixed before any ATLAS reading meant anything [@mackay1992].

links.title: Architectures FORGE must analyze
links.text: TRUSS will generate networks that may not meet FORGE's current requirements, so the two projects have to be developed together.
